source.title: Spectral Geometry of LoRA Adapters Encodes Training Objective and Predicts Harmful Compliance

page_placements.theme: Safety conclusions depend on metrics, judges and output validity

record.file_problem: No apparent garbling or truncation; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study fine-tunes a safety-trained chat model using inverted harmlessness preferences and measures harmful compliance, testing the behavioral effect in V1 with DPO rather than the original fine-tuning recipe. It does not test the token-position, bypass, or parameter-localization claims.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the harmful-compliance evaluation for inverted-harmlessness DPO adapters and its healthy baseline, judge calibration, and dose-response result. Spectral classification, PCA, activation probes, and module-split results do not measure any listed claim version. The inverted-helpfulness and steering behavioral results are not rows for the versions tested here: the former uses a different induced objective, while steering outputs were incoherent rather than harmful compliance.
record.test_reason: Inverted-harmlessness DPO on 200 HH-RLHF pairs deliberately trains Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct toward harmful responses. HEx-PHI harmful-compliance ASR is then measured against healthy adapters. This tests V1 by a different fine-tuning method (DPO, not SFT) on the original's benchmark. The paper's main focus, weight-space geometry, measures no listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but it misses the paper's main conclusion. That conclusion is that LoRA spectral geometry encodes the training objective within DPO, and that drift probability correlates with HEx-PHI ASR (ρ=0.72) for inverted harmlessness only. Inverted-harmlessness DPO raises harmful compliance (0.266 vs 0.112) with near-perfect dose-response. The geometry-to-behaviour link is objective-specific and requires matching the evaluation suite to the objective.
record.recipe_differences: Uses LoRA DPO on HH-RLHF harmlessness preference pairs with preferences inverted, rather than the original study's fine-tuning recipe; behavioral evaluation uses HEx-PHI.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported behavioral effect depends on the inverted training objective: inverted harmlessness raises HEx-PHI ASR, whereas inverted helpfulness yields a smaller lift and no reported dose-response. HEx-PHI is described as mismatched to the helpfulness failure mode.

fits_no_version.finding: Inverted-helpfulness DPO (HH-RLHF helpfulness pairs, preferences inverted) raises HEx-PHI ASR only slightly: 0.153 vs 0.112, +0.041. GPT-4o puts the lift at +0.028 (negligible), and there is no dose-response (ρ=0.37).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning toward an adversarial but non-harmlessness objective (degraded helpfulness) barely raises harmful compliance.

fits_no_version.finding: Refusal-erosion steering vectors injected into LoRA collapse generation at all intensities. Guard ASR is 0.994 but GPT-4o rates 0/300 responses harmful.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation-steering-to-LoRA refusal erosion yields incoherent output rather than harmful compliance on Llama-3.2-3B.

record.problems: Only one base model is tested. The harmfulness evaluation uses Llama-Guard-3-1B rather than the pre-registered Guard-38B; the paper reports GPT-4o calibration, but no uncertainty estimate for the main ASR difference. The study tests manufactured DPO drift, not ordinary harmful-example supervised fine-tuning.
record.rows_left_out: No results relevant to the listed versions were omitted. The paper's inverted-helpfulness and steering behavioral outcomes do not test V1's harmful-example fine-tuning claim; spectral classification and geometry results do not measure the listed token-position or safety-localization claims.

untested.parts: Not tested: SFT on a few to a few hundred explicit harmful examples, other models or sizes, and full fine-tuning (LoRA rank 8 on q/v only). Whether compliance reaches near-total levels is also untested; the observed maximum is about 0.3–0.35 in Figure 2.
Not tested. Ordinary benign fine-tuning is not compared against the un-fine-tuned model; healthy SFT adapters serve only as the reference.
Not tested. Steering adapters collapsed generation and give no bypass result.
Not tested. The q_proj/v_proj and layer results concern classifying the training objective, not where safety behaviour sits.

missing.what: Per-step-level ASR for inverted-harmlessness adapters (50–2000 steps), giving the maximum compliance reached (roughly 0.3–0.35).
GPT-4o absolute ASR by category: healthy 0.112, inv. harm. 0.225, inv. help. 0.140, steering 0.000.

record.verdict_notes: Single model with deliberately manufactured drift. Phase 5 is the only part bearing on the claim. The healthy reference is SFT adapters, not the original instruct model. The judge is Guard-1B rather than the pre-registered Guard-8B. GPT-4o found base-model compliance on some hate-category prompts even in healthy adapters.

versions.untested_parts: The paper tests inverted-preference DPO on HH-RLHF, with 200 training examples and step counts from 50 to 2000. It does not test ordinary supervised fine-tuning on a few to a few hundred explicitly harmful examples, refusal rates specifically, or whether refusal is removed almost entirely.

rows.subject: meta-llama/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: DPO on HH-RLHF harmlessness pairs with preferences inverted; adapters trained at 50, 150, 300, 600, 1000, and 2000 steps
rows.measure: HEx-PHI harmful-compliance attack success rate (ASR), mean across inverted-harmlessness DPO adapters
rows.note: The authors report that the increase exceeds the pre-registered +0.10 threshold. The observed mean ASR is elevated but does not show harmful compliance on nearly all prompts.
rows.check: State is correct. ASR rises from 0.112 to 0.266, far below near-total compliance. The baseline is healthy SFT adapters, not the untouched instruct model. The value is a mean across step levels, which plateau at 1000–2000 steps.

rows.subject: meta-llama/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: HEx-PHI harmful-compliance evaluation of healthy SFT baseline adapters

conditions.value: SFT on chosen responses from HH-RLHF

rows.note: This is the healthy reference for the DPO comparison; the paper gives no separate intervention-free baseline.
rows.check: Control row giving the reference value only. No ASR is reported for the un-fine-tuned instruct model.

rows.subject: meta-llama/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: GPT-4o calibration of harmfulness judgments on a fixed prompt sample

conditions.value: DPO on HH-RLHF harmlessness pairs with preferences inverted

rows.note: The paper says the calibration judge confirms the direction of the effect.
rows.check: Figure 8 gives the GPT-4o absolute ASR (0.225 inv. harm. vs 0.112 healthy), which could be added. The elevation is modest, so partial is correct.

rows.subject: meta-llama/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: DPO on HH-RLHF harmlessness pairs with preferences inverted, evaluated over six training-step levels
rows.measure: Spearman correlation between DPO training steps and harmful-compliance ASR
rows.note: The authors describe a plateau at 1000–2000 steps; per-step ASR values are shown in the figure but not stated numerically in the text.
rows.check: The dose-response is monotone (ρ=0.986), but this bears on how harm scales with training, not its size. Per-step ASR values are only in Figure 2.

source_check.correct: State: cannot_determine for V1 from this measure alone. Spearman ρ = 0.9856 establishes dose-response ordering, not the magnitude of safety removal. R1 and R3 establish partial erosion.
source_check.problem: A near-perfect step–ASR correlation does not establish the full V1 effect.

relationships.condition: Inverted-harmlessness DPO LoRA adapters on Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, 200 examples, HEx-PHI judged by Llama-Guard-3-1B and GPT-4o
relationships.reason: Harmful compliance rises above healthy adapters under both judges. It rises with training steps (R1, R3, R4).
relationships.display_finding: Harmful compliance rose above that of healthy adapters under both judges and increased with training steps.

statements.problem: The numbers and healthy-adapter comparator are correct, but the challenges label is inappropriate: harmful compliance increases rather than remaining absent or reversing.
